text:
marta: Ran the sidecar network-shaping probe on a small slice of dedicated GPU pools in us-west2-A this morning. Quick summary: p95 RPC latency to the model-serv proxies dropped from ~420ms -> ~180ms for noisy-tenant cases, but we saw a ~6% drop in small-batch throughput for <8-token requests. Dashboard: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/sidecar-probes/1766203910

sam: nice, do we have the exact probe config + how we applied shaping?

marta: applied an eBPF-attached sidecar that enforces per-tenant egress rate shaping + burst control. config used:
```yaml
shaper: 
  mode: egress-cgroup
  rate: 250mbit
  burst: 4mb
  priority: tenant-weighted
```
and on host ran: `tc qdisc replace dev eth0 root fq_codel limit 2000` to keep host qdisc sane.

jia: where did the throughput drop show up? GPU utilization? queue latency?

marta: mostly queue latency at the proxy -> runtime handoff. GPU occupancy steady, but small-req worker threads waited ~12-20ms longer on average. Larger batches unaffected.

ran: ops-bot showed an egress token drop spike during the canary window (ops-bot: see logs). Is that due to overly tight burst?

marta: possibly. We tuned burst to 4mb to stop big tenants from blasting KV cache fill traffic. When we tightened to 2mb the p95 improved another ~10ms but small-job tail grew more.

sam: what's the rollback/rollout plan if this hits production? any automatic safety gates?

marta: rollout plan in the canary doc: start 3 nodes in a pool per AZ (us-west2-{a,b,c}), observe 30m of traffic, Gate1: p95 gen latency not degrade by >5% for 95% of tenants, Gate2: small-job throughput degrade <3% across baseline test set. If violation -> automated rollback. Runbook: https://wiki.redwood/internal/ops/sidecar-shaper-runbook

ops-bot: probe-run/1766203910 finished. metrics snapshot attached. Alert thresholds: p95_latency >= 1.1x baseline -> paged.

jia: cost angle? does this increase egress or bandwidth billing?

marta: no change to external egress billing (we're shaping internal host-to-host only). But we did see ~8% higher inter-node retransmits in one rack due to SACK interactions; that translated to an approximate $120/mo extra network spend in that rack if extrapolated. Not material, but worth noting.

sam: any fairness regressions? were low-credit tenants starved?

marta: we used tenant-weighted priorities keyed off committed tiers. In the canary we saw one mid-tier tenant hit a hard limit because their config had an outdated weight (ops ticket TICKET-789). Fixed weight and re-ran canary; behavior normalized. 

ran: should we consider routing some traffic to dedicated nic-shared pools instead of forcing shaping? pros/cons?

marta: tradeoffs: routing to dedicated nic-shared pools reduces need for per-tenant shaping but increases reserved capacity and cost. Shaper allows fine-grained control with less reserved infra. For enterprise tenants wanting guarantees we still offer dedicated pools.

jia: next steps?

marta: 1) expand canary to 5 pools across us-west2-{a,b,c} tomorrow; 2) lower burst incrementally to find sweet spot; 3) add a small-job synthetic test to the CI that catches the 6% regression; 4) follow-up doc with config recommendations for Dedicated vs Shared. I'll open a tracking ticket.

sam: thanks — please ping when the 5-pool canary starts. :thumbsup:

marta: will do. opening ticket now: INC-4521
